text: South Island domestic and industrial users will have their price discounted.
explanation: Price discount policy for South Island users; neutral economic instrument.

text: Labor has done little to educate the public on the benefits of cleaner fuels.
explanation: Performance criticism of Labor's public education efforts on cleaner fuels; no moral vocabulary.

text: In 1997, a single person on the average industrial wage paid 22% of their income in income tax.
explanation: Tax statistic for a single person on the average industrial wage; empirical claim.

text: Together we're the co-leaders of the Green party
explanation: Descriptive statement about Green party co-leadership; no evaluative content.

text: without allowing emissions from aviation to undermine our goal of a zero-carbon Britain by 2050.
explanation: Frames aviation emissions against a zero-carbon target; instrumental environmental policy without explicit moral vocabulary.

text: The development of an ‘alternative growth pole’ along the Atlantic Corridor will be pursued.
explanation: Regional development policy (an 'alternative growth pole' on the Atlantic Corridor); economic/instrumental.

text: This will be underpinned by new rights for patients.
explanation: 'New rights for patients' invokes rights language, which the codebook treats as explicit moral vocabulary (clarification (a) and (d) — affirming rights as moral claims).

text: Current investment in developing and protecting the Australian farm sector does not recognise the large contribution farmers make to our economy.
explanation: Argues current investment fails to recognise farmers' 'large contribution to our economy'; framed as an economic contribution argument, not as moral desert or fairness.

text: We recognize that adoption costs can be high and in some cases prohibitive for families.
explanation: Descriptive acknowledgement that adoption costs can be high or prohibitive; instrumental cost observation without moral-evaluative language.

text: We will increase access to the arts for young people, particularly those of disadvantaged backgrounds,
explanation: Expanding arts access for young people from disadvantaged backgrounds; per the negative clarification, equality-of-access commitments framed instrumentally without explicit moral vocabulary are coded 0.

text: Direct this new spending to health, education, and a few carefully targeted initiatives.
explanation: A neutral directive about allocating spending across sectors; purely instrumental budgetary language with no moral vocabulary or evaluative terms, fitting the negative clarification on descriptions of funding and programmes.

text: The Green Party is committed to bringing rail services into public ownership and control.
explanation: A straightforward policy commitment on public ownership of rail; no moral-evaluative language, just an administrative/structural position, per the negative clarification on neutral policy descriptions.

text: provide direct and meaningful support to land managers in delivering ecoservices; | and
explanation: Describes a support mechanism for land managers delivering ecoservices; 'meaningful' is a generic positive adjective without moral content, so it falls under the negative clarification on instrumental programme language.

text: and providing other services as required, thus contributing to Ireland’s political and economic well being.
explanation: Instrumental statement about services contributing to political and economic well-being; no moral vocabulary, matching the negative clarification on administrative/economic descriptions.

text: • Conflicting roles and responsibilities.
explanation: A terse administrative observation about conflicting roles; no evaluative or moral content.

text: An SNP government will strive to ensure that Scotland becomes a world leader in securing a sustainable environment
explanation: An aspirational goal (world leader in sustainable environment) lacking explicit moral vocabulary; fits the negative clarification on aspirational visions without moral-evaluative language.

text: With the investment that we are promising in hospital buildings,
explanation: A fragment about promised investment in hospital buildings; a funding commitment with no moral language.

text: The question that should still be asked of Labor is:
explanation: A rhetorical question fragment directed at an opponent; contains no moral vocabulary or evaluation.

text: And with new laws to crack down on domestic violence,
explanation: Although domestic violence is a morally charged subject, the text treats it instrumentally (new laws to 'crack down') with no moral-evaluative terms like 'intolerable' or 'wrong'; per the negative clarification on descriptive references to morally charged subjects, this is 0.

text: Fine Gael will support the on-going nationwide roll out of the “Food Dudes” Fruit and Vegetable Promotion programme to all primary schools in Ireland.
explanation: Support for a school fruit and vegetable promotion programme; instrumental programme commitment with no moral vocabulary, like the negative example on sports participation.

text: Every board shall publish before March of each year an annual report on  its own activities as opposed to the wider work of the state body.
explanation: An administrative reporting requirement for boards; purely procedural with no moral content.

text: In particular, as we expand access to talking therapies we expect many more people to recover and be able to seek work again.
explanation: Describes an instrumental policy outcome (expanding talking therapies so people can return to work); framed in pragmatic labour-market terms with no moral vocabulary, matching the negative clarification on equality-of-access arguments framed purely instrumentally.

text: and free up  resources  for whānau development.
explanation: Resource reallocation for whānau development; instrumental language without moral-evaluative terms.

text: We will give 1 weeks paid Parental leave for either parent to take, giving them more choice.
explanation: A parental leave policy framed around parental choice; 'choice' here is a policy feature, not an appeal to freedom as a protected value, and no moral vocabulary appears.

text: Policy alignment will ensure the wise use of public dollars.
explanation: Efficiency argument about wise use of public dollars; fits the negative clarification on fiscal/value-for-money arguments.

text: At £1.4 Trillion, that equates to £54,353 per household;
explanation: A statistical/fiscal claim converting debt to a per-household figure; empirical content without moral evaluation.

text: maintain the Defence Forces’ proud reputation in peacekeeping
explanation: 'Proud reputation' is a generic positive descriptor about an institution's standing, akin to the negative clarification's 'successful, thriving' adjectives; no explicit moral vocabulary about rights, justice, or virtue is invoked.

text: The Nationals are determined to eliminate the divide between those living in and those living outside major capital cities, including any limitation on access to a fair legal system that respects the rights and responsibilities of all Australians.
explanation: Uses explicit moral vocabulary: 'fair legal system', 'respects the rights... of all Australians', and frames eliminating a geographic 'divide' as an imperative; matches clarification (a) on fair/rights language.

text: These moves will eliminate remaining inequality in the income tax system and enhance its progressive nature.
explanation: Commitment to 'eliminate remaining inequality' invokes equality as a moral value and frames remaining inequality as a wrong to be removed, per clarification (a) and (c), even though it sits within tax policy.

text: It is now enshrined in law that we must pay 0.7 per cent of our Gross National Income (GNI) on aid every year.
explanation: States a legal requirement to spend 0.7% of GNI on aid; 'must' reflects a statutory obligation, not a moral imperative, and the text is a factual description of law with no moral-evaluative vocabulary.

text: Caroline Lucas and housing In July 2014 Caroline Lucas MP introduced a Housing (Affordability, Supply and Tenant Protection) Bill to highlight the problems faced by private tenants.
explanation: Factual description of an MP introducing a housing bill to 'highlight problems'; descriptive of legislative activity with no explicit moral language.

text: Support for 2,500 additional aged care beds;
explanation: A spending commitment for aged care beds; a neutral programme/funding item per the negative clarification.

text: Develop new community policing structures, through local policing forums in individual communities, to reconnect the Gardaí and local communities in a spirit of genuine partnership.
explanation: Proposes community policing structures and partnership between Gardaí and communities; 'spirit of genuine partnership' is institutional, not moral, vocabulary; instrumental policy design.

text: We will: save you money by cutting government waste
explanation: Saving money by cutting government waste; a fiscal/efficiency argument explicitly listed in the negative clarification.

text: Ireland should be the best place in the world to grow up, and to grow old.
explanation: An aspirational slogan ('best place in the world to grow up, and to grow old') with only generic positive evaluation ('best'); fits the negative clarification on aspirational visions lacking moral vocabulary.

text: Ministerial Cars: We will end the automatic entitlement to a State car for every Government Minister.
explanation: Ending automatic entitlement to ministerial state cars; an administrative/perk reform described neutrally without moral framing.

text: If you can’t trust Labour and National to go public about poisoned baby milk then what on earth can you trust them on.
explanation: A partisan attack questioning opponents' trustworthiness over poisoned baby milk; while it touches a morally charged subject, it functions as a partisan slogan about political trust, with no explicit moral vocabulary from the codebook (justice, rights, dignity); coded 0 per the negative clarification on partisan attacks lacking moral vocabulary.

text: All TDs will be entitled to put forward proposals for legislation and a lottery at the start of each session will determine which Bills will be debated.
explanation: Describes a procedural lottery mechanism for selecting Bills; neutral institutional design with no moral content.

text: We will put in train preparations for the 100th anniversary of the Easter Rising, in a manner that honours the contribution of the men and women of Easter Week,
explanation: Committing to mark the Easter Rising centenary 'in a manner that honours the contribution of the men and women of Easter Week' expresses moral desert and patriotic reverence — honour/respect for national forebears; per clarification (b) on virtue language including patriotism, this is moral-evaluative language, though I note it is a boundary case since it concerns a commemorative plan.

text: We will support sensible immigration policies that meet our economic needs
explanation: Immigration policy justified by 'economic needs'; instrumental economic framing, 'sensible' being a generic adjective; no moral vocabulary.

text: Establishing the right accountability framework for schools.
explanation: Accountability framework for schools; 'right' here means appropriate/correct, not a moral right; administrative language per the negative clarification.

text: Republicans share President Bush's understanding that just as events in Europe determined the outcome of the Cold War, events in the broader Middle East will set the course for the victory of free nations in the War on Terror.
explanation: Invokes 'free nations' and 'War on Terror' — an appeal to freedom as a value whose victory is at stake, plus vice language ('terror'); the clarification explicitly includes appeals to freedom/liberty and lists 'terror' as vice language.

text: • there is appropriate time for debate to be conducted.
explanation: Procedural point about time for debate; administrative with no moral-evaluative content.

text: All recreational fishers should help police the system to ensure that there is no room for poachers and quasi ‘recreational’ fishers who sell or raffle their catches.
explanation: Enforcement appeal against poaching and illegal sale of catches; framed as rule-compliance/policing with no explicit moral vocabulary.

text: •  Created  2000 jobs  during the recession  through state housing upgrades.
explanation: Claims job creation through housing upgrades; an economic performance statistic per the negative clarification.

text: Constitutional stability for Northern Ireland;
explanation: Constitutional stability is a governance aspiration stated without moral vocabulary.

text: It will dismantle the dysfunctional Health Service Executive (HSE) that was created by Micheál Martin in 2004,
explanation: Pledge to dismantle a 'dysfunctional' agency; 'dysfunctional' is a generic negative adjective about performance, like the negative clarification's 'burdensome', not a moral judgment.

text: conflicts with long-term strategies to cut waste volumes by recycling and reduction, requires huge scale to operate efficiently and generates large volumes of traffic.
explanation: Technical arguments against a waste facility (scale, efficiency, traffic); instrumental environmental/planning reasoning with no moral language.

text: and transition to a prosperous, decarbonized economy.
explanation: Transition to a 'prosperous, decarbonized economy'; 'prosperous' is a generic positive adjective and the framing is economic/technocratic, per the negative clarification.

text: This will support our aim to make Britain the best place in Europe, and one of the top five worldwide, to do business by 2020.
explanation: Competitiveness goal of making Britain a top place to do business; economic aspiration without moral vocabulary.

text: The Nationals believe that, when wealth is generated in a region, a fair share of the resulting government revenue should be returned to that region and to regional Australia more generally.
explanation: Explicitly invokes a 'fair share' of revenue for regions — 'fair' is explicit moral vocabulary per clarification (a), framing revenue distribution as a matter of fairness.

text: Half a million of us regularly play sport, while 400,000 volunteer as coaches, match officials and referees.
explanation: Participation and volunteering statistics for sport; factual claims with no evaluative moral content.

text: We recognise the contribution that Mäori enterprise and entrepreneurship has made to our nation's economy.
explanation: Acknowledges Māori enterprise's contribution to the economy; a descriptive recognition framed in economic terms without moral-evaluative vocabulary like respect, dignity, or desert.

text: We will: Work to secure the full implementation of the Military Covenant in Northern Ireland.
explanation: A commitment to implement the Military Covenant; the text itself is an instrumental implementation pledge with no moral vocabulary (no mention of duty, honour, or desert).

text: abolish the current 2% limit for funding political parties, which acts against new and smaller parties and could be seen as supporting the status quo;
explanation: Argues the funding cap 'acts against' smaller parties and supports the status quo; this is a descriptive claim about effects rather than explicit moral vocabulary (it does not say unfair or discriminatory), so it is 0, though it borders on a fairness argument.

text: After so long in office, Mr Howard has forgotten what fairness actually means.
explanation: Explicit use of 'fairness' — accusing Mr Howard of forgetting what fairness means is a direct appeal to moral vocabulary per clarification (a).

text: • develop Parents as First Teacher (PAFT) programmes across the country.
explanation: Programme development commitment (Parents as First Teacher); instrumental education policy with no moral language.

text: We will crackdown on overseas producers who don’t cooperate with anti-dumping investigations
explanation: Trade enforcement pledge against non-cooperative overseas producers; instrumental economic/compliance framing without moral vocabulary.

text: Labour will ensure that the Defence  Forces are appropriately equipped and staffed to meet Ireland’s  obligations to United Nations and EU peacekeeping missions.
explanation: Commitment to equip Defence Forces for UN/EU peacekeeping obligations; 'obligations' is institutional/legal, and the text is a capacity pledge without moral-evaluative language.

text: Processing of applications and decision-making is subject to long delays, while the absence of legislation means there is frequent resort to the Courts for judicial review.
explanation: Describes administrative delays and litigation frequency in application processing; a neutral description of administrative dysfunction per the negative clarification.
